subject: general
question: A bank offers 7.8% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits ₹9,920 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ______ (give your answer correct to 2 decimal places).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Half-yearly rate** (r) = 7.8% ÷ 2 = 3.9%.

**Effective rate** for 1st deposit (2 periods) = 3.9 + 3.9 + (3.9 × 3.9)/100 = 7.9521%.

**Effective rate** for 2nd deposit (1 period) = 3.9%.

**Total Interest %** = 7.9521% + 3.9% = 11.8521%.

**Interest gained** = 9920 × 11.8521 ÷ 100 ≈ ₹1,175.73.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,175.73.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹9,920 each on **1 January** and **1 July**.

**Annual Rate (R)** = 7.8% | **Half-yearly rate (r)** = 7.8% ÷ 2 = 3.9%.

**Time:** End of the year (31 December).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e4960c9e9cb6a3440da3218848ffff004bb36d9db1a4f87c20d0f4bb860d82a.png] 

**Step 1: Interest on 1st deposit (1 Jan) for the first 6 months:**

⇒ I₁ = 9920 × (3.9 ÷ 100) = ₹386.88

⇒ Amount on 1 July = 9920 + 386.88 = ₹10,306.88

**Step 2: Interest on this amount for the next 6 months:**

⇒ I₂ = 10306.88 × (3.9 ÷ 100) = ₹401.96832

**Step 3: Interest on 2nd deposit (1 July) for remaining 6 months:**

⇒ I₃ = 9920 × (3.9 ÷ 100) = ₹386.88

**Step 4: Total Interest Gained:**

⇒ Total Interest = I₁ (on 1st) + I₂ (on 1st) + I₃ (on 2nd)

⇒ Total Interest = 386.88 + 401.96832 + 386.88 = ₹1,175.72832

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places = ₹1,175.73

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,175.73.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding Formula

When interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the formula becomes A = P[1 + (R/2)/100]²ⁿ, where R is the annual rate and n is the number of years.

Effective Rate of Interest

The **effective annual rate** for compounding can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: a + b + (ab/100).

Interest Calculation Tip

For multiple deposits at different times, calculate interest for each **principal** separately based on its duration in the account.
